newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to slightly higher in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.75/0.70 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 0.45/0.40 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.43/1.38 percent against 1.15/1.10 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.33/99.38 from Tuesday's close of S$99.28/99.33.
September 2001 was unchanged from Tuesday's close of S$97.38/97.43 and June 2003 unchanged at S$95.38/95.43.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent versus Tuesday's 3 2-7/8 percent.
